abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease in which disease onset is influenced by genetic, age-associated and environmental factors. Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life and may provide a molecular link between aging and neuronal vulnerability. Here, we investigated neuronal somatic mutational patterns in ALS and control motor cortex using three previously generated 10X single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing datasets. Within the genomic regions accessible to 10X sequencing, variant calls showed established features of neuronal somatic mutagenesis, including neuronal enrichment, age-associated accumulation and recovery of the clock-like SBS5 mutational signature. ALS was associated with a disease-specific age-dependent trajectory of neuronal somatic mutation burden, with higher burden in younger ALS donors and a decreasing difference with age. SBS5 represented the largest fitted mutational component and showed a corresponding age-dependent difference. A similar pattern was observed in an independent single-cell whole-genome sequencing dataset. These findings support age-dependent alterations in neuronal somatic mutational patterns in ALS.
